1.explanation:
• docs/reveal/index.qmd – shows how revealjs slides are generated and how custom content (including HTML divs) is handled in the slideshow format.  
• docs/Syntax Test.qmd – contains core tests of fenced div syntax (::: blocks) to verify how Markdown constructs are parsed into HTML containers.  
• docs/callouts.qmd – demonstrates nested block handling (callout blocks use similar fenced div syntax), valuable for comparing how text-only blocks vs image-containing blocks render.  
• docs/crossrefs/figure-syntax-div.qmd – tests placing figures (images with captions) inside divs; helps isolate whether the issue is specific to images vs figures.  
• docs/crossrefs/figure-syntax-img.qmd – focuses on bare image syntax, showing correct vs incorrect placement inside containers.  

Together these examples expose how fenced div parsing and HTML generation treat image elements differently in revealjs and help reproduce and debug the container-wrapping bug.
1.bug_scenario: The issue arises when the user wraps an image in a generic fenced div (e.g. :::{.qrcodeblock} … :::) in a revealjs slide. In Test A and Test C (the custom and outer div examples), the Markdown text (“Oh hello” and “Why not?”) remains inside the div, but the image itself is “bumped” outside the div container—rendering below the div rather than between the two lines of text. Only in the column layout (Test B) does the image stay inside its intended container. This suggests that the revealjs output engine treats images differently in arbitrary divs versus columns, causing unexpected HTML wrapping.
